questions.question: In which of the following years was the Mughal empire established by Babur?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1526
  • Fact: The Mughal empire was established by Babur after the First Battle of Panipat.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Hindustan Republic Association?
questions.solution:
• Person: Ram Prasad Bismil
  • Fact: He was a key founder of the Hindustan Republic Association (HRA) in 1924.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Swami Dayanand Saraswati is INCORRECT?
questions.option_3: He was the founder of Brahmo Samaj.
questions.option_4: He was the founder of Arya Samaj.
questions.solution:
• Incorrect Statement: 'He was the founder of Brahmo Samaj'
  • Correction: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded Arya Samaj; Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Second Round Table Conference in London held?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1931
  • Event: The Second Round Table Conference was held in London, attended by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: Who among the following had written Kitab-ul-Hind that gave an incisive description of early 11th Century India?
questions.solution:
• Author: Al-Biruni
  • Work: Kitab-ul-Hind, which provided an incisive description of early 11th Century India.

questions.question: Veer Surendra Sai was a freedom fighter from:
questions.solution:
• Origin: Odisha
  • Fact: Veer Surendra Sai was a revolutionary freedom fighter against British rule from this state.

questions.question: The Mysore Palace was the residence of the ______.
questions.solution:
• Residence: Wodeyars
  • Fact: The Mysore Palace was the official seat of the Wodeyar dynasty.

questions.question: Who among the following assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London?
questions.solution:
• Person: Madan Lal Dhingra
  • Fact: He assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London (1909).

questions.question: Which of the following Acts introduced federal features and provincial autonomy in the legislature and also made provisions for the distribution of legislative powers between the Centre and the provinces?
questions.solution:
• Act: The Government of India Act, 1935
  • Impact: Introduced provincial autonomy and federal features in the legislature.

questions.question: Who among the following economists coined the terminology 'Hindu Rate of Growth'?
questions.solution:
• Economist: Raj Krishna
  • Term: Coined 'Hindu Rate of Growth' to describe the low growth rate of the Indian economy.

questions.question: Which of the following Buddhist sites is located in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
• Location: Sarnath
  • Fact: A major Buddhist site in Uttar Pradesh where Buddha gave his first sermon.

questions.question: Chandernagore (Chandannagar) was a ______ colony captured by the British Navy on 23 March 1757.
questions.solution:
• Colony: French
  • Fact: Chandernagore was a French establishment captured by the British Navy in 1757.

questions.question: The Sun Temple of Odisha was built in the 12th Century AD by which of the following emperors?
questions.solution:
• Emperor: Narasimha Deva I
  • Fact: The Eastern Ganga ruler who built the famous Sun Temple of Odisha.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the All-India Harijan Sevak Sangh founded?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1932
  • Organization: All-India Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian to unfurl the tricolour on foreign land?
questions.solution:
• Person: Bhikaiji Cama
  • Fact: The first Indian to unfurl the Indian tricolour on foreign soil (Germany, 1907).

questions.question: Which of the following is the meaning of ‘Pishtaq’ in the context of medieval Indo-Islamic architecture?
questions.solution:
• Architecture: Tall gateway
  • Term: Pishtaq refers to the formal arched gateway in Indo-Islamic buildings.

questions.question: Which of the following is a work on statecraft written by Krishnadevaraya?
questions.solution:
• Work: Amuktamalyada
  • Author: Krishnadevaraya; the book is a famous Telugu work on statecraft.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1947?
questions.solution:
• Nizam: Osman Ali
  • Context: He was the last Nizam of Hyderabad during India's independence in 1947.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the origin and enactment of the Indian Age of Consent Act passed?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1891
  • Act: The Indian Age of Consent Act was passed to regulate the age of marriage/consent.

questions.question: The place of Gautama Buddha’s birth was a grove known as ______.
questions.solution:
• Birthplace: Lumbini
  • Fact: Gautama Buddha was born in this grove located in modern-day Nepal.

questions.question: ______ organised his trusted nobles into a group of forty known as Turkan-i-Chahalgani.
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Iltutmish
  • Group: He formed the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (Group of Forty) trusted nobles.

questions.question: Who among the following had written the book ‘Char Chaman’, during the reign of Shah Jahan, describing the Mughal nobility?
questions.solution:
• Author: Chandrabhan Brahman
  • Work: Char Chaman, which described the Mughal nobility under Shah Jahan.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers is called the ‘Napolean of India’?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Samudragupta
  • Title: Often called the 'Napoleon of India' due to his military brilliance.

questions.question: Who among the following laid the foundations of the Indian National Movement by founding the Indian Association at Calcutta in 1876?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Surendranath Banerjee
  • Event: Founded the Indian Association at Calcutta in 1876.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the revolt in the countryside of the Bombay Deccan occur?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1875
  • Event: The Deccan Riots (peasant revolt) broke out in the Bombay Deccan.
